title: Article 224 — Appointment of additional and acting Judges

content.overview: Article 224 provides that if by reason of any temporary increase in the business of a High Court or by reason of arrears of work, it appears to the President that the number of Judges should be temporarily increased, the President may appoint duly qualified persons to be additional Judges for a period not exceeding two years. When a Judge (other than an additional Judge) is absent or unable to perform duties, or is appointed acting CJ, the President may appoint a duly qualified person as an acting Judge. Additional and acting Judges hold office until the period expires or the age of 62, whichever is earlier, and are not taken into account for certain permanent-strength purposes.
content.glance: President may appoint additional Judges (≤2 years) for temporary increase/arrears; acting Judges when a Judge is absent/unable or acting as CJ.
content.study:
Article 224:
(1) Additional Judges: temporary increase in business or arrears → President may appoint qualified persons for a period not exceeding two years.
(2) Acting Judges: when any Judge (other than additional) is absent/unable or appointed to act as CJ → President may appoint a qualified person to act as Judge until the permanent Judge resumes or the acting-CJ appointment ends.
Age limit 62 applies; additional/acting tenure ends earlier if the period ends.

Examination: additional vs acting; 2-year cap for additional; qualifications same as permanent; age 62.

sections.heading: Two categories
sections.body:
1. Additional Judges: temporary increase/arrears; period not exceeding 2 years.
2. Acting Judges: when a Judge is absent/unable or acting as CJ.
Both: duly qualified; office until period ends or age 62, whichever earlier.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When may additional and acting Judges of a High Court be appointed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 224, if by reason of temporary increase in business or arrears of work it appears to the President that the number of Judges of a High Court should be temporarily increased, the President may appoint duly qualified persons to be additional Judges for a period not exceeding two years. When any Judge other than an additional Judge is absent or unable to perform duties, or is appointed to act as Chief Justice, the President may appoint a duly qualified person to act as a Judge of the Court until the permanent Judge resumes duties or the acting-CJ arrangement ends.

examTips: Additional ≤2 years for arrears/increase; acting when Judge absent or acting CJ.

keyTakeaways: Art 224: additional and acting HC Judges.
